question: Can a frozen defective candidate be inserted at VERT's generated-candidate slot without changing its oracle or harness?
selection_reason: VERT ships a median-of-three benchmark with the same three-scalar, return-value observation shape as S14.

changes: Replaced only the f_gold body inside the existing LLM Output delimiters with S14's minimum-of-three computation widened from u8 to VERT's deposited i32 signature.

official_cli_attempt.rustc_bootstrap_outcome: link failure because the generated command requires the unavailable gold linker
official_cli_attempt.action: stopped without installing an undocumented linker or changing VERT

root_cause.candidate_side: The Bolero harness writes PARAM1, PARAM2, and PARAM3 and calls the Rust candidate with all three dynamic values.
root_cause.reference_side: The deposited rWasm wrapper injects only PARAM1. Its call to the C-derived function retains constants 2 and 29 for the second and third arguments.

interpretation: The minimal external-candidate injection compiles, but it cannot produce a valid S14 detection because VERT's deposited multi-argument wrapper does not give the C/Wasm and Rust sides the same logical input. The untouched correct candidate fails identically. Per the frozen-baseline policy, the wrapper and tool setup were not repaired; the pilot is unscored and VERT remains unsupported for the 36-pair comparison.

single_parameter_native_control.purpose: Separate VERT's checker sensitivity in its native one-scalar envelope from applicability to the frozen 36-pair corpus.

changes: Replaced only the generated Rust f_gold body: the deposited candidate computes x + 1 and the injected incorrect candidate returns x.

single_parameter_native_control.interpretation: With one scalar argument, VERT's deposited oracle and Bolero harness distinguish a correct candidate from an injected incorrect candidate. This establishes checker sensitivity only inside VERT's native generated-project format. It is not one of the frozen 36 defects and does not change the scored applicability result.

apparent_counterexamples.basis: The released wrapper synchronizes only PARAM1. The Rust candidate receives all dynamic arguments, so these are not relational comparisons over the same input; the untouched correct S14 control fails identically.

completed_comparison.basis: Its audited one-scalar contract wrapper fits VERT's native input envelope, but the release-mode run completes without exposing the free(NULL) defect.

all_36_intake.end_to_end_reading: All 36 frozen pairs were submitted through one fixed external adapter without repairing VERT. VERT validly completed one comparison and missed it; all other pairs stopped before a valid result. End-to-end detection is 0/36.
